scope: Proposition 9.5 (Lower-barrier initialization) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 100. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the following assertions for arbitrary deterministic cost normalizations and the same fixed buffered tests. (a) Every sequence of finite-cost crossing witnesses has a subsequential certificate retaining a fixed positive spatial advance. The common-kernel and annulus transfer properties hold in these limits. (b) At unscaled cost, the largest projected advance of every path using at most k edges tends to zero in probability, for each fixed k, uniformly in the compact testing region. (c) A winding circuit used in Xj contains a subpath tested by a fixed finite collection of these crossing tests. The probability and cost thresholds have strict margins, so failure of their high-probability lower test retains a finite-cost witness with probability bounded away from zero. Then, for the finite circuit quantiles in Equation (9.1), lim sup j→∞ j−1 log4 Aj ≥ p.
